item.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty. Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.” , The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. item.title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
item.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk. In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances. “I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.” He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said. – ‘What changed?’ – Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports. And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing. Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return. Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.” Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress. item.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
item.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. item.title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday. ﻿ President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled. “Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o . We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd. Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.” After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.” ‘Follow Who Know Road’ President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country. “You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars. “The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added. Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people. Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections. The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State. During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support. The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections. Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. item.title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos. The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.” She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.” Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.” In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang. The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.” Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.” He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.” Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.” He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.” Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations. The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026. The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday. The post Gov. Mutfwang loses brother appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
item.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. item.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
item.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSG suffer major injury blow as Doue, Kvaratskhelia face long layoffs
item.description: The sight of the unfortunate Desire Doue going down holding his knee in agony was distressing for anyone connected to Paris Saint-Germain, but encouraging for those hoping to stop the French club from winning a third consecutive Champions League this season. PSG have been European champions in each of the last two years and their quest to retain the crown this season has started superbly, with four straight wins leaving them top of the 36-team standings halfway through the league phase. However, they have now lost the outstanding Doue, exactly a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia succumbed to the same injury, casting serious doubt over the chances of Luis Enrique’s team going all the way again. Doue was stretchered off in tears after twisting his knee awkwardly during PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday, with the club later confirming the 21-year-old had ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and needed surgery. Doue’s season is likely now over, while Kvaratskhelia is beginning the process of rehabilitation after rupturing the same ACL in last month’s win over Barcelona. The explosive Georgian winger was the best player in last season’s Champions League knockout rounds and came sixth in this year’s Ballon d’Or ranking. Meanwhile Doue was the man of the match when Paris demolished Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 Champions League final and had been their star performer in recent weeks. “He will come back twice as strong. I am not worried,” insisted Luis Enrique, but he will know that the injuries to two of his best attacking players seriously damage the club’s prospects of more European glory. So what do they do now, as they prepare to host Roma on Wednesday and with the January transfer window approaching? “We are always open to possibilities in the transfer window, but not just because we have players injured,” said the Spaniard. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem.” He could be forgiven for now regretting the decision to allow Bradley Barcola — scorer of 34 goals across the last two campaigns — to leave for Liverpool. Suddenly the pressure on the injury-prone Ousmane Dembele to stay fit is enormous. – Bayern in bother – As for who appears the best-placed to take advantage of PSG’s misfortune, it may not be Bayern Munich, as the German champions deal with problems of their own. Twenty-four hours before Doue went down for PSG, newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was substituted with an ankle injury playing for Bayern against Cologne. He is now expected to be sidelined for up to four months, although that will at least mean he has a chance of being fresh by March, in time for the Champions League knockout rounds. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season,” Kane said in a social media post. item.title: Sinner set to undergo knee surgery, might miss Australian Open
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former world number one Jannik Sinner is set to undergo knee surgery in Finland, a development that could rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open, according to Sky Sports Italia. The Italian tennis star could be sidelined for between three and four months following the procedure, which is expected to be performed by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in tendon and muscle injuries. Sinner, 25, has been struggling with persistent inflammation in his right knee, which forced him to end his 2026 season prematurely. His last competitive appearance was at Wimbledon in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final to win his fifth Grand Slam title. He subsequently missed the North American hard-court tournaments, including the US Open, because of the injury. The former world number one had earlier expressed hope of returning to action at the Australian Open in January, following a planned appearance at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in late December. “The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” Sinner told reporters in Milan earlier this month. However, the reported surgery and expected recovery period have cast serious doubt over his participation in the season’s first Grand Slam. Despite competing in only nine tournaments during the 2026 season, Sinner recorded 44 wins in 47 matches, won six titles and reclaimed the world number one ranking during a 30-match winning streak. He also won his maiden titles at Indian Wells, Monte Carlo and Madrid, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to win all nine ATP Masters 1000 tournaments. Sinner ended his season in October and recently announced his separation from coach Darren Cahill after a successful five-year partnership. Magnus Norman has been tipped to replace the Australian. item.title: ‘Three of my supporters were killed’ – LG chair reacts to Omo-Agege’s assassination claim
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi, Ochuko Akuopha, Akpokona Omafuaire & Efe Onodjae UGHELLI – Olorogun Jaro Egbo, the local government chairman of Ughelli North, Delta State, were Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said an assassination attempt was made on his life, has said three of his (Egbo) supporters were killed. Among those reportedly killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. Also, former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and reportedly battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention. The latest bloodshed, which has triggered a fierce exchange of accusations between Omo-Agege’s camp and Olorogun Egbo, is the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state. Clashes had erupted in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was also killed. While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the other of instigating the violence. The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence. item.title: Alleged assassination: We want IG to investigate, not Delta police — Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice. Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. He alleged that police officers present during the incident failed to intervene as gunmen opened fire on his team, adding that the attack had heightened fears among opposition politicians in the state. “What we have learned is this: we are not safe here in Delta State. In fact, all members of the opposition party, NDC, most especially, we are all endangered,” he said. Omo-Agege claimed that six truckloads of policemen were deployed to the campaign venue but did not act when the shooting occurred. He accused the state police command of being unlikely to conduct an impartial investigation and urged the IGP to handle the case directly. “We do not expect any justice to come from the police here in Delta State. Neither do we expect any justice to come from the police on this very one,” he said. “We are appealing to the IG to take this matter over directly. We tried to reach him this evening. We couldn’t reach him.” The former lawmaker said he wanted the federal police leadership to investigate the incident, insisting that the state command should not be involved in the probe. He also called for justice for those affected by the attack, saying lives had been lost and several others were receiving treatment in hospitals. “We need justice. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” Omo-Agege said. Despite the incident, he vowed not to abandon his campaign, dismissing suggestions that the attack could intimidate him into withdrawing from the race. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very big mistake and a big lie. Ain’t going to happen,” he said. He, however, appealed to his supporters to remain calm and avoid reprisals, warning that tensions remained high following the attack. item.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. item.title: Delta imposes curfew in Ughelli North after deadly violence
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area following reports of deadly violence and gunshots in parts of the council. The curfew, which takes effect on Monday, November 23, 2026, will run daily from 6pm to 6am until further notice. The Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, announced the restriction in a statement, saying the measure was aimed at restoring calm and bringing the security situation under control. According to the statement, the curfew covers the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area. The government urged residents to comply strictly with the directive. The development follows reports of deadly violence in the area, including an attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign tour of Uduere. The attack reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured. The post Delta imposes curfew in Ughelli North after deadly violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Navy intercepts 89,000 litres of stolen crude, illegal diesel in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence. In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil. He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres. “The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said. The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta. It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.
